title: A finitely generated field extension becomes separably generated after finite purely inseparable extensions
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension] (i.e. $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$). Then there exist a field $K'$ with a field homomorphism $K\to K'$, and a subfield $k'\subseteq K'$ containing the image of $k$ under $k\to K\to K'$, such that $k'/k$ and $K'/K$ are finite purely inseparable extensions [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] and $K'$ is separably generated over $k'$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1): there is a transcendence basis $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of $K'/k'$ with $K'/k'(x_i;i\in I)$ separable algebraic. In other words there is a commutative square of field extensions $k\to k'\to K'$, $k\to K\to K'$ with $k'/k$, $K'/K$ finite purely inseparable and $K'/k'$ separably generated.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962) and its proof (induction on $[K:K_{sep}]$ over $k(x_1,\dots,x_r)$, using Fields, Lemma fields-lemma-separable-first; one step marked 'details omitted')

proof.text: (Characteristic $0$.) Suppose $k$ has characteristic $0$. Since $K$ is finitely generated over $k$, $K$ itself is a finitely generated subextension of $K/k$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable] it has a transcendence basis $x_1,\dots,x_r$ with $K/k(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ separable algebraic: $K$ is separably generated over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1). Take $K'=K$ with the identity $K\to K'$ and $k'=k$: the extensions $k/k$ and $K/K$ are finite (dimension $1$) and purely inseparable (in characteristic $0$ this means equality) [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and the square commutes. From now on $k$ has characteristic $p>0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: first sentence ('only interesting when the characteristic of k is p > 0')

proof.text: (Set-up and the inductive claim.) For a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finitely generated extension $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ and a finite transcendence basis $x=(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], put $E_x=k(x_1,\dots,x_r)\subseteq K$. Each $a_i$ is algebraic over $E_x$ (definition of transcendence basis) and $K=E_x(a_1,\dots,a_n)$, so $K/E_x$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension]. Let $K_s\subseteq K$ be the separable algebraic closure of $E_x$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] (applied to the algebraic extension $K/E_x$), $K_s$ is a subfield containing $E_x$, $K_s/E_x$ is separable algebraic, and every $\gamma\in K$ has $\gamma^{p^n}\in K_s$ for some $n\ge0$. Since $E_x\subseteq K_s$, an $E_x$-basis of $K$ spans $K$ over $K_s$, so $d(K,k,x):=[K:K_s]$ is a finite integer $\ge1$. We prove by strong induction on $e\ge1$ the claim $C(e)$: for every field $k$ of characteristic $p$, every finitely generated $K/k$ and every finite transcendence basis $x$ of $K/k$ with $d(K,k,x)=e$, there are $k'$, $K'$ as in the lemma. By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] every finitely generated $K/k$ has a finite transcendence basis $x$, so the claims $C(e)$ for all $e$ give the lemma.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: 'Choose x_1, ..., x_r a transcendence basis ... the extension k(x_1, ..., x_r) ⊂ K is finite. Let K/K_sep/k(x_1, ..., x_r) be the subextension found in Fields, Lemma 030K ... We will use induction on d = [K : K_sep]'

proof.text: (The case $e=1$.) If $d(K,k,x)=1$ then $K=K_s$, so $K/k(x_1,\dots,x_r)$ is separable algebraic and $x$ is a transcendence basis: $K$ is separably generated over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1). Take $k'=k$, $K'=K$ (identity maps); $k/k$ and $K/K$ are finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] (every element is its own $p^0$-th power). This proves $C(1)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: 'If K = K_sep then we are done.'

otin K_s$. For the least such $n$ put $ eta=\gamma^{p^{n-1}}$: then $ eta\in K$, $ eta
otin K_s$ and $\alpha:= eta^p\in K_s$. As $K_s/E_x$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], the minimal polynomial $P=T^m+c_1T^{m-1}+\dots+c_m\in E_x[T]$ of $\alpha$ over $E_x$ is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial], i.e. coprime to $P'$; hence $P$ has pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure (a double root $ho$ would give a common factor $T-ho$ of $P$ and $P'$, while $\gcd(P,P')=1$ in $E_x[T]$ stays $1$ over any extension by a B'ezout identity).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: 'Assume that d > 1. Choose a β ∈ K with α = β^p ∈ K_sep and β ∉ K_sep. Let P = T^n + a_1T^{n-1} + ... + a_n be the minimal polynomial of α over k(x_1, ..., x_r).'

proof.text: (The step marked 'details omitted': $k'$ and $E'$.) Fix an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and view $K\subseteq\Omega$. For $c\in\Omega$ the polynomial $T^p-c$ has a root in $\Omega$, unique because the Frobenius $u\mapsto u^p$ of $\Omega$ is an injective ring homomorphism [def-weil-ring-frobenius]; write it $c^{1/p}$. Since $x_1,\dots,x_r$ are algebraically independent over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], every element of $E_x$ is $f(x)/g(x)$ with $f,g\in k[X_1,\dots,X_r]$, $g(x)\ne0$ (these quotients form a subfield of $K$ containing $k$ and the $x_i$, and lie in every such subfield). Write $c_j=f_j(x)/g_j(x)$ ($j=1,\dots,m$) and $h_j=f_jg_j^{p-1}$, so $c_j=h_j(x)/g_j(x)^p$. Let $S\subseteq k$ be the finite set of coefficients of $h_1,\dots,h_m$, and put $k'=k(s^{1/p};s\in S)\subseteq\Omega$ and $E'=k'(x_1^{1/p},\dots,x_r^{1/p})\subseteq\Omega$. Then $E_x\subseteq E'$ (as $k\subseteq k'$ and $x_i=(x_i^{1/p})^p$). For $h_j=\sum_I s_IX^I$ let $\tilde h_j=\sum_I s_I^{1/p}\prod_i(x_i^{1/p})^{I_i}\in E'$; since the Frobenius of $\Omega$ is a ring homomorphism, $\tilde h_j^p=\sum_I s_Ix^I=h_j(x)$. Hence $c_j=(\tilde h_j/g_j(x))^p$: every coefficient of $P$ is a $p$-th power in $E'$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: 'Let k'/k be a finite purely inseparable extension obtained by adjoining pth roots such that each a_i is a pth power in k'(x_1^{1/p}, ..., x_r^{1/p}). Such an extension exists; details omitted.'

proof.text: (Adjoining $p$-th roots is finite purely inseparable.) Let $F\subseteq\Omega$ be a subfield and $\beta_1,\dots,\beta_t\in\Omega$ with $\beta_i^p\in F$. The set $\{\gamma\in\Omega:\gamma^p\in F\}$ is a subfield of $\Omega$ (the Frobenius is a ring homomorphism [def-weil-ring-frobenius], and $(\gamma^{-1})^p=(\gamma^p)^{-1}$) containing $F$ and all $\beta_i$, so every $\gamma\in F(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_t)$ has $\gamma^p\in F$; each $\beta_i$ is algebraic over $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] (a root of $T^p-\beta_i^p$), so $F(\beta_1,\dots,\beta_t)/F$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], hence finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. With $F=k$ and the $s^{1/p}$: $k'/k$ is finite purely inseparable and $k'^p\subseteq k$. Let $L\subseteq\Omega$ be the compositum of $K$ and $E'$ (the smallest subfield containing both); as $k\subseteq K$, $L=K(s^{1/p},x_1^{1/p},\dots,x_r^{1/p};s\in S)$ with $s,x_i\in K$, so with $F=K$: $L/K$ is finite purely inseparable. This is the diagram of the source with $L$ the compositum.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: 'k'/k be a finite purely inseparable extension obtained by adjoining pth roots ... Let L be a field fitting into the diagram ... We may and do assume L is the compositum of K and k'(x_1^{1/p}, ..., x_r^{1/p})'

proof.text: ($x^{1/p}$ is a transcendence basis of $L/k'$.) (a) $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ and $k\subseteq k'$ give $L=k'(x_1^{1/p},\dots,x_r^{1/p},a_1,\dots,a_n)$: $L/k'$ is finitely generated. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-compositum-degree-bound] with $F=E_x\subseteq K$, $E_x\subseteq M=E'$ (step 5) and $KE'=L$: $L/E'$ is finite with $[L:E']\le[K:E_x]$; hence $L$ is algebraic over $E'$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] (for $\lambda\in L$ the powers $1,\lambda,\lambda^2,\dots$ are linearly dependent over $E'$). (c) The $x_i^{1/p}$ are algebraically independent over $k'$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]: if $G\in k'[X_1,\dots,X_r]$ is nonzero with $G(x^{1/p})=0$, let $G^{(p)}$ be $G$ with every coefficient raised to the $p$-th power; its coefficients lie in $k$ (step 6: $k'^p\subseteq k$), it is nonzero (the Frobenius of $k'$ is injective), and $G^{(p)}(x)=G(x^{1/p})^p=0$ because the Frobenius of $\Omega$ is a ring homomorphism [def-weil-ring-frobenius], contradicting the algebraic independence of $x$ over $k$. By (b) and (c), $x^{1/p}=(x_1^{1/p},\dots,x_r^{1/p})$ is a finite transcendence basis of $L/k'$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] with $k'(x^{1/p})=E'$, and $k'$ has characteristic $p$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: implicit in 'By induction we can find k' ⊂ k'' and L ⊂ L' as in the lemma for the extension L/k'' (the induction is applied to L/k' with the transcendence basis x_1^{1/p}, ..., x_r^{1/p})

proof.text: ($\beta$ becomes separable.) Let $L_s\subseteq L$ be the separable algebraic closure of $E'$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]; by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] (step 7: $L/E'$ is algebraic) $L_s$ is a subfield containing $E'$ and $L_s/E'$ is separable algebraic. Every $\kappa\in K_s$ lies in $L_s$: its minimal polynomial $Q$ over $E_x$ is separable, the minimal polynomial $Q_1$ of $\kappa$ over $E'\supseteq E_x$ divides $Q$, and a divisor of a separable polynomial is separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial] (if $Q=Q_1R$ then $Q'=Q_1'R+Q_1R'$, so a common factor of $Q_1,Q_1'$ divides $Q$ and $Q'$). In particular $\alpha\in L_s$ and $K_s\subseteq L_s$. Now $P\in E_x[T]\subseteq E'[T]$ has $P(\alpha)=0$, pairwise distinct roots in an algebraic closure (step 4) and all coefficients $p$-th powers in $E'$ (step 5), so [lem-weil-pbc-separable-root-pth-power] applied to the separable algebraic extension $L_s/E'$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] gives $\alpha'\in L_s$ with $\alpha'^p=\alpha$. Then $(\beta-\alpha')^p=\beta^p-\alpha'^p=0$ in the field $L$ [def-weil-ring-frobenius], so $\beta=\alpha'\in L_s$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: 'Let L/L_sep/k'(x_1^{1/p}, ..., x_r^{1/p}) be the subextension found in Fields, Lemma 030K. Then L_sep is the compositum of K_sep and k'(x_1^{1/p}, ..., x_r^{1/p}). The element α ∈ L_sep is a zero of the polynomial P ... By Fields, Lemma 031V we see that α = (α')^p for some α' ∈ L_sep. Clearly, this means that β maps to α' ∈ L_sep.'

proof.text: (The degree drops.) Put $K_1=K_s(\beta)\subseteq K$. By step 8, $K_1\subseteq L_s$, and $E'\subseteq L_s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-compositum-degree-bound] in $\Omega$ with $F=K_1\subseteq K$ ($K/K_1$ is finite, as $K/E_x$ is finite and $E_x\subseteq K_1$) and $K_1\subseteq M=L_s$: the compositum $KL_s$ is contained in $L$ and contains $K$ and $E'$, hence equals $L$, and $[L:L_s]\le[K:K_1]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity], $e=[K:K_s]=[K:K_1]\,[K_1:K_s]$ with $[K_1:K_s]\ge2$ because $\beta\notin K_s$. Hence $d(L,k',x^{1/p})=[L:L_s]\le e/2<e$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated, line 9962), proof: 'In other words, we get the tower of fields ... Thus this construction leads to a new situation with [L : L_sep] < [K : K_sep].'

proof.text: (Induction and conclusion.) By steps 6, 7 and 9, $L/k'$ is a finitely generated extension in characteristic $p$ with the finite transcendence basis $x^{1/p}$ and $d(L,k',x^{1/p})<e$, so the induction hypothesis $C(d(L,k',x^{1/p}))$ gives a field $L'$ with a field homomorphism $L\to L'$ and a subfield $k''\subseteq L'$ containing the image of $k'$, such that $k''/k'$ and $L'/L$ are finite purely inseparable and $L'$ is separably generated over $k''$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (1). Put $K'=L'$ with $K\to L\to L'$ (inclusion followed by $L\to L'$). The image of $k$ lies in that of $k'\subseteq L$, hence in $k''$, and $k\to k''$ is the composite $k\subseteq k'\to k''$, so the square commutes. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-transitive], the towers $k\subseteq k'\subseteq k''$ (step 6 and the induction) and $K\subseteq L\subseteq L'$ (step 6 and the induction) give that $k''/k$ and $K'/K$ are finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; and $K'/k''$ is separably generated. This proves $C(e)$, and with steps 2 and 3 the lemma.
